about.title: Burlingame Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Burlingame residents rely on all sorts of products every day, from kitchen appliances in homes along Chapin Avenue to power tools used by contractors near California Drive. When a product is designed poorly, built with a flaw, or sold without adequate warnings, the people who use it can be seriously hurt through no fault of their own. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was defective, not on proving carelessness by the manufacturer. LawProactive is a free service that connects Burlingame residents with an independent attorney who understands how these claims work, including the importance of preserving the product and any packaging as evidence. We're not a law firm, and we never guarantee results, but we can help you take a clear next step after a product injury, whether it happened at home, at work, or somewhere in between.

whyChoose.title: Why Burlingame Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Focus
items.desc: California's strict liability standard generally means you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and caused your injury. An attorney can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer that sold the product in Burlingame can potentially be held responsible. This gives you more than one avenue to pursue when a defective product causes harm.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Guidance
items.desc: Keeping the product, its packaging, and any related receipts intact after an injury is often critical to a claim. An independent attorney can advise you early on how to protect this evidence before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective rather than on the manufacturer's conduct. An attorney can evaluate whether a design, manufacturing, or warning defect applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me in Burlingame?
items.answer: Try to preserve the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, and any receipts. Avoid attempting repairs or discarding it, since this evidence can be important for an independent attorney reviewing your claim.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Burlingame with independent attorneys who handle product liability cases. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
